title: RN start of care, patient with cognitive decline, son answers

turns.text: Hello Mr. Kim, I'm Dana, your nurse from the home health agency. Peter, thanks for being here.
Of course. Dad, this is the nurse.
Hello, hello.
Can you tell me your birthday, Mr. Kim?
Nineteen forty... forty.
It's July 22nd, 1938, Dad. He mixes it up.
Thank you. What language does he prefer to use?
Korean at home. With doctors he speaks English, it's fine, and I'm always there.
So no interpreter needed for appointments?
No, he doesn't want one.
Is he of Hispanic or Latino origin?
No.
And his race?
Korean.
What's covering home health, original Medicare or an Advantage plan?
Original Medicare. And he still has a retiree health plan from his old company.
Who lives here with him?
Me. I moved in last year. But I work days at the plant, seven to five, so he's on his own during the day. Evenings and nights I'm here.
Mr. Kim, I am going to say three words for you to remember. Please repeat the words after I have said all three. The words are sock, blue, and bed. Now tell me the three words.
Sock... and bed. Sock and bed.
Thank you. Please tell me what year it is right now.
Two thousand twenty-three.
What month are we in right now?
June, I think. It's warm.
And what day of the week is today?
Wednesday. Peter's bowling night is Wednesday.
Before he got sick this last time, how was he with bathing, dressing, the toilet, eating?
He ate and used the toilet on his own, but I helped him shower and with buttons. So partly.
Walking from room to room before?
He walked on his own, slow, but on his own.
Stairs?
We have three steps at the front door. I'd hold his arm on those.
And planning things, remembering his medicine, shopping?
I do all of that. The pills are in a locked box, I hand them to him.
Did he use any equipment before, a walker, a wheelchair?
A regular wheelchair for long trips, like the doctor's office. No walker.
How many times has he been in the hospital since spring?
This is the third time since April. Heart failure each time.
Have you noticed any change in his memory or mood lately?
He's been a lot more confused the last couple of months. He used to know the date, always.
Let's go through his medications.
Warfarin, insulin twice a day, donepezil, metoprolol, furosemide, potassium, and a stool softener.
Mr. Kim, over the past 5 days, how much of the time has pain made it hard for you to sleep at night?
Pain? No. No pain.
He hasn't complained about any pain at all this week.
Does he get short of breath? When?
Walking to the bathroom, it's maybe fifteen feet, he has to stop and catch his breath. Sitting, he's okay.
Mr. Kim, how often do you feel lonely or isolated from those around you?
Often. Since my wife died. Peter works.
Let's get your weight and height.
Okay, the scale says one forty-two point five. And he's five foot five?
Five five, yes.
That's all for the assessment. I'll call the doctor about his breathing.

notes: Not discussed, must abstain: J0530 (skipped because J0510 is 0, no pain). Traps: caregiver corrects the birth year; 2023 is missed by 3 years (code 1); June vs September is missed by more than a month (code 0); son is home nights only (code 08); 142.5 rounds up to 143.
